# Datacenter Buildouts and Brazilian Equities

Report 199 | Published 2026-10-11 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2026-10-11/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/199.json)

Datacenter spending, bond yields and Brazilian equity risk.

The most testable call worked: a left-wing runoff victory was followed by a sharp Brazilian selloff. The local yield-peak call also received near-term support. The long-term Brazil thesis remains open, while the explanation of SLR reform confuses leverage capital with risk-weighted capital.

**Coverage:** Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.

## Claims

### 199-C01

**AI investment crowds out other borrowers.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | ai-capex-crowding-out |
| Source blocks | 7, 9, 10, 18 |
| Thesis family | ai-capex-crowding-out |

Competing demand can raise financing costs, but construction divergence does not identify a causal crowding-out effect. Treasury advisers subsequently reported no evidence of crowding out Treasury or nontechnology borrowing; physical resources, financing and policy effects should be tested separately.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [September private construction spending](https://www.census.gov/construction/c30/pdf/privsa.pdf) | Census Bureau | 2026-11-02 | Verified in the audit

Data centers +90.3% year over year; manufacturing -17.9%; computer/electronics/electrical manufacturing -41.7%. Figures are annualized spending flows, not accumulated productive capacity.

- [Treasury borrowing advisory minutes](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0680) | U.S. Treasury | 2026-11-04 | Verified in the audit

Committee presentation found no evidence yet of crowding out Treasury or nontechnology borrowing.

### 199-C08

**Reserve purchases slowed without becoming stimulus.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | gradual-print-2026 |
| Source blocks | 26, 27, 28, 32, 37 |

The New York Fed explicitly framed purchases as reserve management, with higher initial purchases ahead of April tax flows. Assets rose only about $47.6bn from April 29 to October 7 and were nearly flat thereafter. The operational distinction is supported; it does not prove purchases have no market effects.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Reserve management purchase announcement](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/opolicy/operating_policy_251210a) | New York Fed | 2025-12-10 | Verified in the audit

Purchases began December 12, 2025 to maintain ample reserves; initial monthly amount about $40 billion. Technical reserve supply does not itself establish a change in the interest-rate stance.

- [Early experience with reserve management purchases](https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/speeches/2026/per260326) | New York Fed | 2026-03-26 | Verified in the audit

The Desk purchased about $40 billion monthly ahead of expected April tax flows. The objective was maintaining ample reserves.

- [WALCL observations through the audit cutoff](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/WALCL) | FRED / originating statistical agency | Verified in the audit

April 29:$6.699950tn; October 7:$6.747560tn; November 4:$6.748145tn.

### 199-C10

**SLR relief changes risk-weighted Treasury treatment.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | slr-versus-risk-weighted-capital |
| Source blocks | 35, 36 |
| Thesis family | slr-versus-risk-weighted-capital |

This conflates separate capital constraints. The supplementary leverage ratio is a non-risk-based backstop; reducing its requirement is not a change in Treasury risk weights. A relevant e SLR reform had already been finalized in November 2025 and taken effect in April 2026, though additional future changes remain possible.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Final enhanced leverage-ratio rule](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/bcreg20251125b.htm) | Federal Reserve, FDIC and OCC | 2025-11-25 | Verified in the audit

Leverage capital standard acts as a backstop to risk-based requirements. Final rule adopted November 2025, effective April 2026, with optional January adoption.

### 199-C14

**Brazil combines high real rates with external buffers.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | brazil-real-yields-external-balance |
| Source blocks | 61, 64 |
| Thesis family | brazil-real-yields-external-balance |

The central bank confirms a 13.75% policy rate. Official balance-of-payments data distinguish the goods surplus from the current-account deficit, correcting an earlier report’s conflation. Nominal policy rate minus trailing inflation is an ex-post shortcut, not the expected real return of a foreign investor; reserve adequacy needs short-term obligations and currency composition.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Policy-rate history](https://www.bcb.gov.br/controleinflacao/historicotaxasjuros?jet_blog_ajax=1&nocache=1775980985) | Banco Central do Brasil | 2026-09-16 | Verified in the audit

September 16 decision set the policy rate at 13.75%.

Shows a goods surplus alongside a current-account deficit, and distinguishes reserves, conventional external debt and intercompany loans.

## Framework lessons

- A conditional election forecast can be resolved separately from the long-term investment thesis.
- Specify which capital constraint is binding before predicting the effect of regulatory relief.

## Verification limitations

- Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
- A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
- Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
